hints: Look carefully at limonene and count how many C=C double bonds can react, remembering that excess means every alkene will be attacked.
Recall that dry HCl adds by electrophilic addition with H going to the carbon that already has more H, leaving the more stable tertiary carbocation for Cl to join.
Apply that Markovnikov pattern to both the ring alkene and the side-chain alkene, placing Cl on the most substituted carbon in each case.
walkthrough:
**Spot the two alkenes**

Limonene has two separate C=C bonds. One is trisubstituted inside the six-membered ring, the other is the terminal $C(CH_3)=CH_2$ group on the side chain.

Because HCl is in excess, both double bonds will undergo addition:
$$2 \times (C=C + HCl \rightarrow CH-CCl)$$

**Remember Markovnikov addition**

Dry HCl adds as $H^+$ then $Cl^-$. $H^+$ adds first to make the most stable carbocation.

That means H adds to the carbon with more H already, and Cl ends up on the more substituted, tertiary carbon.

**Apply to each double bond**

For the ring $C=C$, H adds to the $CH$ end and Cl adds to the $C-CH_3$ end to give a tertiary chloride at the top.

For the side chain $(CH_3)C=CH_2$, H adds to the $CH_2$ end and Cl adds to the central carbon to give $(CH_3)_2CCl$ at the bottom. Both Cl atoms are on tertiary carbons.

options.A: This shows correct Markovnikov addition to the ring alkene only. It is the product with one equivalent of HCl, but with excess HCl the side-chain alkene must also react, so this is incomplete.
options.B: This shows Cl on a secondary carbon of the ring and no reaction of the side chain. It reverses Markovnikov selectivity and ignores the excess reagent, so both features are wrong.
options.C: This shows Markovnikov addition at both alkenes. Both Cl atoms are on tertiary carbons, the top ring $C(Cl)CH_3$ and the bottom $C(Cl)(CH_3)_2$, exactly what excess HCl gives.
options.D: This places Cl on the less substituted carbons, a primary $CH_2Cl$ at the bottom and a secondary CHCl in the ring. This is anti-Markovnikov addition via the less stable carbocations, so it will not be the major product.
